clinical_knowledge.topic: Post-Thoracotomy Pain Syndrome (Intercostal Neuralgia) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Post-Thoracotomy Pain Syndrome (Intercostal Neuralgia) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Post-Thoracotomy Pain: Gabapentin, topical lidocaine patches, intercostal nerve block, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: chronic burning pain along incision line 3 months after surgery

Key HPI features: A 74-year-old female presents to the clinic with chronic burning pain along incision line 3 months after surgery. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Post-Thoracotomy Pain.
Relevant background/PMH: Thoracotomy 3 months ago, otherwise unremarkable
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Post-Thoracotomy Pain Syndrome (Intercostal Neuralgia).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Wound infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Fever or wound drainage — suggests infection instead of neuralgia.
management_principles: Plan for Post-Thoracotomy Pain: Gabapentin, topical lidocaine patches, intercostal nerve block
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Chronic nerve pain along a surgical incision from intercostal nerve injury during thoracic surgery, persisting well beyond normal wound healing.
differentials: Recurrent disease at the surgical site
red_flags: Fever or wound drainage — suggests infection instead of neuralgia

must_ask.say: How many months ago was your chest surgery?
Does the pain feel burning or electric, along the incision line?
Does the incision look normal, or is there any redness or drainage?
Does touching the area or certain movements make it worse?
How is this pain affecting your daily activities?
